**Service Name:** MindWell Sleep Study

**Summary:** The MindWell Sleep Study is a research project that uses a sleep-tracking app and a wrist sensor to study the effects of the app on insomnia. Here's a breakdown of the key provisions:

* **Purpose:** The study aims to examine how well a sleep-tracking app works for people with insomnia.
* **Participation:** Participants will wear a wrist sensor for 8 weeks and complete a weekly survey.
* **Risks:** The main risk involved is minor skin irritation from the sensor strap.
* **Data Sharing:** De-identified data (data that doesn't personally identify individuals) may be shared with other universities, but personal data will not be shared outside of the research team. 
* **Withdrawal:** You can withdraw from the study at any time without facing any penalty.
* **Compensation:** Participants will receive $75 after completing the study.

**Clauses to be aware of:**

* While data sharing with other universities is allowed, identifiable data will not be shared outside the study team. This is a good thing, but if you're concerned about data privacy, you may want to review the study's data protection policies.
* There is no mention of what happens to personal data once the study is complete, so it's unclear what happens if a participant withdraws after a few weeks.

Overall, these Terms of Service seem to be relatively straightforward, but if you have any questions or concerns, you should contact the Institutional Review Board (IRB) at irb@example.edu.
source_tos:
INFORMED CONSENT — MINDWELL SLEEP STUDY

1. PURPOSE. This study examines the effects of a sleep-tracking app on insomnia.
2. PROCEDURES. Participants wear a wrist sensor for 8 weeks and complete weekly surveys.
3. RISKS. Minimal risk: skin irritation from the sensor strap.
4. DATA. De-identified data may be shared with collaborating universities. Identifiable data will not be shared outside the research team.
5. WITHDRAWAL. You may withdraw at any time without penalty.
6. COMPENSATION. Participants receive $75 upon completion.
7. CONTACT. For questions contact the IRB at irb@example.edu.

**Service Name:**
The Terms of Service, also known as the Microsoft Services Agreement, applies to the products and services described on Microsoft's official terms page.

**Key Provisions:**

* **Scope**: These terms govern your relationship with Microsoft, which includes various products and services.
* **Content and License**: When you submit content, such as photos or text, Microsoft can use it to improve its services, train AI/ML systems, and operate its services.
* **Privacy**: Microsoft's published Privacy Policy defines the types of personal data it collects and how it processes it.
* **Dispute Resolution**: Most disputes will be resolved through **binding arbitration** (a private dispute process instead of court), with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts. Some users may be required to use class-action waivers, which can limit your ability to participate in group lawsuits.
* **Termination**: Either party can end the agreement, subject to specified conditions.
* **Contact**: You can reach out to Microsoft for questions about these terms.

**Clauses to Consider:**

* **Content and License**: Microsoft can use your submitted content as it sees fit, subject to your settings and applicable law. This means you should review Microsoft's usage policies and adjust your settings accordingly.
* **Dispute Resolution**: The use of binding arbitration and class-action waivers may limit your ability to resolve disputes in a traditional court of law.
* **Termination**: Microsoft can terminate the agreement at any time, which may impact access to your account or services.

Remember that these terms are subject to change, and Microsoft has made updates to the agreement, including the addition of a new 'exportable data' subsection and changes to Xbox service-specific terms. Always review the most up-to-date version of the Microsoft Services Agreement for the latest information.
source_tos:
SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — MICROSOFT SERVICES AGREEMENT (Effective 2025; replaces the 2024 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with Microsoft and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2025 version differs from the 2024 version in the following ways: Added a new 'exportable data' subsection under Your Content, clarified that some services may have separate support terms, added language that some trial offers may require auto-renewal, and updated Xbox service-specific terms regarding sign-in to non-Microsoft platforms. Documented in Microsoft's Updates page (servicesagreement/Updates).
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by Microsoft to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/servicesagreement/ . The previous version is available at https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/servicesagreement/upcoming.aspx .

**Microsoft Services Agreement (2023 → 2024)**

These terms apply to the relationship between you and Microsoft, covering all Microsoft products and services mentioned on the company's official terms page.

Some key provisions to note:

* **Content and License**: Microsoft uses your user-submitted content to improve their services, including training their AI/ML systems. However, this only happens after considering your settings and applicable law. 
* **Privacy**: The terms reference Microsoft's individual **Privacy Policy**, which explains the types of personal data collected and how it's handled.
* **Dispute Resolution**: If you have a problem with Microsoft, you'll need to resolve the issue through **binding arbitration (a private dispute process instead of court)**, unless you opt-out within 30 days for new accounts. This clause means you may not be able to pursue a lawsuit in court.
* **Termination**: Either party can end the agreement under specified conditions.
* **Contact**: If you have questions about these terms, you should check Microsoft's published contact information on their terms page.

Concerning terms include:
* **Dispute Resolution (Section 5)**: This clause makes Microsoft less accountable to users in the event of conflicts.
source_tos:
SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — MICROSOFT SERVICES AGREEMENT (2023 → 2024) (Effective 2024; replaces the 2023 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with Microsoft and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2024 version differs from the 2023 version in the following ways: Added clarifications around moderation/enforcement with a link to external policy pages, expanded Xbox section to address third-party platforms tracking and sharing user data, and updated the kids-on-Xbox subsection regarding family settings on third-party platforms.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by Microsoft to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/servicesagreement/Updates . The previous version is available at https://web.archive.org/web/2023*/https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/servicesagreement/ .

[EXPECTED SUMMARY POINTS]
- The updated terms take effect in 2024 and replace the 2023 version.
- Key change: Added clarifications around moderation/enforcement with a link to external policy pages, expanded Xbox section to address third-party platforms tracking and sharing user data, and updated the kids-on-Xbox subsection regarding family settings on third-party platforms.

- Users should review the cross-referenced Privacy Policy to understand data handling.
- The previous version of the terms is available for comparison at https://web.archive.org/web/2023*/https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/servicesagreement/.

**Service Name:** The OpenAI Terms of Use (Consumer)

**Summary:** This Terms of Service document governs your relationship with OpenAI, a company that creates Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Machine Learning (ML) systems. The updated version (2024) outlines how you can use OpenAI's products and services, how they use your content, how to resolve disputes, and when your agreement can be terminated.

**Key Provisions:**

* **Scope:** These terms apply to the specific products and services listed on OpenAI's official terms page.

6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.

**Service Name:** OpenAI Services Agreement (Business/API)

These Terms of Service outline the agreement between you and OpenAI for using its business and API services. Here's a simplified breakdown of the key provisions:

**Key Provisions:**

* **Scope:** These terms apply to OpenAI's products and services, including ChatGPT Enterprise, ChatGPT Team, and the API.
* **Data Handling:** OpenAI uses user-submitted content to improve and train its AI/ML systems. However, this usage is subject to your settings and applicable law.
* **Indemnification:** You agree to hold OpenAI harmless from any claims, losses, or liabilities that arise from your use of the services.
* **Service Level Agreements (SLAs):** These agreements outline the expected performance of OpenAI's services. However, the details of the SLAs are not explicitly stated in this version of the Terms of Service.
* **Dispute Resolution:** You and OpenAI will use binding arbitration (a private dispute process instead of court) to resolve disputes, with some exceptions (such as Steam, which has opted out of arbitration).
* **Termination:** Either party can terminate the agreement under certain conditions, which are not detailed in this summary.
* **Contact Information:** You can find the company's contact information for questions about the terms at [https://openai.com/policies/services-agreement/](https://openai.com/policies/services-agreement/).

**Harmful Clauses:**

* The **indemnification clause** may be problematic if you're using OpenAI's services in a way that's protected by consumer rights or other laws. This clause could potentially limit your options for seeking recourse if something goes wrong.
* **Binding arbitration** might be unfavorable if you're looking for a more traditional court process to resolve disputes.

**Important Note:** These Terms of Service are subject to change, and OpenAI may update them at any time. Make sure to review the live document for the most up-to-date information.

Keep in mind that these terms are a plain-language summary, and you should review the full document for the latest details and fine print.
source_tos:
SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — OPENAI SERVICES AGREEMENT (BUSINESS/API) (Effective 2025; replaces the 2024 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with OpenAI and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2025 version differs from the 2024 version in the following ways: Replaced the prior Business Terms with a single OpenAI Services Agreement effective May 31, 2025, covering API, ChatGPT Enterprise, ChatGPT Team and other business services, with updated provisions on data handling, indemnification and SLAs. Announcement: community.openai.com/t/new-openai-services-agreement-effective-may-31-2025/1249405.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by OpenAI to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://openai.com/policies/services-agreement/ . The previous version is available at https://web.archive.org/web/2024/https://openai.com/policies/business-terms/ .

**Service Name:** Anthropic Consumer Terms of Service

The Anthropic Consumer Terms of Service outline the agreement between you as a user and Anthropic, the company providing its products and services, such as Claude.ai, Claude Pro, and Claude apps.

**Key Provisions:**

* **Relationship**: These terms govern your relationship with Anthropic, specifying which services and products are included.
* **What Happens to Your Content**: You're allowing Anthropic to use your submitted content to improve and train its AI/ML systems, subject to your settings and applicable law.
* **Data Protection and Privacy**: The terms reference Anthropic's published Privacy Policy, which explains what personal data is collected and how it's processed.
* **Dispute Resolution**: Most updated terms require binding arbitration (a private dispute process instead of court) with class-action waivers, although there's a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts.
* **Termination**: Either party can end the agreement with the conditions described in the live document.
* **Contact**: If you have questions about these terms, check the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL.

**Potential Concerns:**

* **Data Ownership**: The terms allow Anthropic to use your submitted content, including personal data, without specifying precise limits or ownership responsibilities.
* **Binding Arbitration and Class-Action Waivers**: This could limit your ability to join a class-action lawsuit and enforce your rights through the courts, even if the dispute is relatively minor.
* **Lack of Prior Version**: As this is the first available version, it's uncertain how these terms were different from previous versions, potentially raising questions about potential retroactive changes or inconsistencies.

SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — ANTHROPIC CONSUMER TERMS OF SERVICE (Effective 2025; replaces the 2024 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with Anthropic and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2025 version differs from the 2024 version in the following ways: Updated effective October 8, 2025: clarified scope (Claude.ai, Claude Pro, Claude apps), added explicit Acceptable Use Policy reference, refined provisions on business/enterprise email-domain linking, and updated dispute-resolution and governing-law sections. Versioning tracked at tostracker.app/document/anthropic.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by Anthropic to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://www.anthropic.com/legal/consumer-terms . The previous version is available at https://web.archive.org/web/2024/https://www.anthropic.com/legal/consumer-terms .

**Summary:** These terms describe the relationship between you (a user) and Anthropic, a company that provides AI and ML systems. The terms cover use of the company's products and services, how your data is used, and what happens when there's a dispute.

**Key Provisions:**

* **Scope**: These terms apply to the company's products and services, as listed on their official terms page.
* **Content and License**: Anthropic can use your submitted content to improve and train their AI systems, as long as you've allowed it. This means that the work you give them can be used to train their models, potentially benefiting others who use the same service.
* **Privacy**: The terms mention the company's Privacy Policy, which explains how your personal data is collected and processed.
* **Dispute Resolution**: You'll need to go through binding arbitration (a private dispute process instead of court) to resolve disputes, with some exceptions. For 30 days from opening a new account, you can opt-out of arbitration.
* **Termination**: Either party can terminate the agreement under certain conditions.

**Flags on potentially Harmful Clauses:**

* The dispute resolution process may be less favorable to users, as it involves binding arbitration with class-action waivers.
* If you don't carefully set your data usage settings, Anthropic might be able to use your data for model training without your explicit consent.
* The termination clause may allow the company to stop providing services without providing detailed reasons or notice.

**Important Information:**
- You can contact the company for questions about these terms at the address listed on their website.
- The old version of the terms is available at an archived URL.
source_tos:
SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — ANTHROPIC COMMERCIAL TERMS OF SERVICE (API) (Effective 2024; replaces the 2023 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with Anthropic and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2024 version differs from the 2023 version in the following ways: Added more detailed sections on customer data and outputs, clarified that customer prompts and completions are not used to train models by default, and updated indemnification and acceptable-use language tied to the published Usage Policy.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by Anthropic to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://www.anthropic.com/legal/commercial-terms . The previous version is available at https://web.archive.org/web/2023/https://www.anthropic.com/legal/commercial-terms .

**Service Name:** Meta (previously Facebook) Terms of Service.

These terms provide the rules for using Meta's products and services. Here are the key provisions:

**Using Meta's Products Implies Agreement**: By using Meta's products, you're agreeing to these terms.

**Content License**: When you upload content to Meta's products, you're giving the company a license to use it. However, this license is subject to your account settings and applicable laws.

**Data Collection and Processing**: Meta collects and processes user data (see their published Privacy Policy) for operating, improving, and enhancing their services.

**Dispute Resolution**: Most disputes will be resolved through **binding arbitration (a private dispute process instead of court)** with **class-action waivers (you can't be part of a larger group lawsuit)**. You have a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts.

**Termination**: Either Meta or you can stop using their services at any time, subject to certain conditions.

**Key Provision of Concern**:

- **Binding Arbitration and Class-Action Waivers**: This provision may limit your ability to seek group relief or go to court.
- **Data Collection and Processing**: While Meta's Privacy Policy outlines data collection and processing, users should be mindful of how their data is used.
- **Termination Condition**: The text implies termination may be subject to unspecified conditions, which could be concerning if users don't understand the grounds for termination.

These concerns arise because the Terms outline significant powers given to Meta and limitations placed on users. It's essential to understand and review these terms thoroughly when using Meta's products. If you have specific questions or want more clarity on particular points, consult Meta's published legal contact information.
source_tos:
SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — FACEBOOK / META TERMS OF SERVICE (Effective 2025; replaces the 2024 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with Meta (Facebook) and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2025 version differs from the 2024 version in the following ways: Effective January 1, 2025: tightened opening agreement language ('using these products means you agree'), added clearer license framing for content uploaded to Meta Products, and added wording about Meta's use of AI/machine-learning systems on user content for service improvement and safety.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by Meta (Facebook) to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://www.facebook.com/terms . The previous version is available at https://web.archive.org/web/20240101000000*/https://www.facebook.com/terms .

**Service Name:** Instagram Terms of Use and Privacy Policy.

These Terms of Service govern your relationship with Meta (the company behind Instagram), explaining how you can use the service, what happens to your content, and what to expect from the company.

**Key Provisions:**

* **Scope**: These Terms apply to all products and services listed on Meta's official terms page.
* **Content and License**: You grant Instagram a non-exclusive license to use your content worldwide, which includes editing and training AI/ML systems.
* **Privacy**: Instagram cross-references its published Privacy Policy, explaining how it collects and processes your personal data.
* **Dispute Resolution**: In case of disputes, binding arbitration (a private dispute process instead of court) is required, with some exceptions. You can opt-out of this requirement within 30 days of creating an account.
* **Termination**: Either party can terminate the agreement if certain conditions are met.
* **Contact**: For questions about the Terms, you can refer to the company's published legal contact information.

**Flags for Harmful Clauses:**

* The requirement for binding arbitration (Clause 5) means that any disputes will be resolved privately instead of through the court system. This can make it more difficult for users to seek redress if something goes wrong.
* The license you grant to Instagram (Clause 3) allows the company to use and modify your content, including for AI/ML training, which may be unsettling for users who value their photos or other content.
* The company's ability to terminate the agreement (Clause 6) gives Instagram some flexibility to end the relationship if it chooses to do so. However, it's unclear how this impacts users who have invested significant time and effort into their profile or content.

Keep in mind that these Terms are subject to change, and users are expected to review the updated Terms regularly. It's essential to be aware of what you're agreeing to when using Instagram, especially when it comes to your content and data.
source_tos:
SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — INSTAGRAM TERMS OF USE (Effective 2025; replaces the 2024 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with Meta (Instagram) and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2025 version differs from the 2024 version in the following ways: Aligned with the Meta umbrella update effective January 1, 2025: explicit grant of a worldwide non-exclusive license to use, distribute and modify uploaded content, and new wording referencing AI features and data processing across Meta Products.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by Meta (Instagram) to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://help.instagram.com/581066165581870 . The previous version is available at https://web.archive.org/web/20240101000000*/https://help.instagram.com/581066165581870 .

Keep in mind that this is a simplified explanation, and you should review the full Terms of Service for specific details and requirements.

SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — X TERMS OF SERVICE (Effective 2024; replaces the 2023 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with X (Twitter) and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2024 version differs from the 2023 version in the following ways: Effective November 15, 2024: added an explicit, royalty-free, worldwide license for X to use posted content for training machine-learning and generative-AI models, removed the prior in-product opt-out language, and broadened third-party data-sharing permissions.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by X (Twitter) to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://x.com/en/tos . The previous version is available at https://web.archive.org/web/20240515000000*/https://twitter.com/en/tos .

**Service Name:** TikTok Terms of Service (US).

**Summary:** The Terms of Service, effective 2026, set out the rules governing the user's relationship with TikTok. The terms cover how TikTok uses user-submitted content, data collection and processing, dispute resolution, termination, and contact information.

**Key Provisions:**

* **Scope:** The terms apply to TikTok's products and services as described on the company's official terms page.
* **Content and License:** TikTok uses user-submitted content to operate, improve, and train its AI/ML systems, subject to user settings and applicable law.
* **Privacy:** The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which explains personal data collection and processing.
* **Dispute Resolution:** Most users are required to participate in binding arbitration (a private dispute process instead of court) with class-action waivers. New accounts have a 30-day opt-out window.
* **Termination:** Either party may terminate the agreement under certain conditions.
* **Contact:** Users can find information about the terms and contact the company through the published legal contact information at [https://www.tiktok.com/legal/page/us/terms-of-service/en](https://www.tiktok.com/legal/page/us/terms-of-service/en).

**Clauses that may be harmful to the user:**

* **Binding arbitration:** This may require users to resolve disputes outside of a court system, potentially limiting their access to a jury trial or appeal.
* **Class-action waivers:** Users may not be able to join a class-action lawsuit to pursue claims on behalf of a group of individuals.
* **Generative-AI rules:** TikTok says their AI output should be treated as-is, but users are still responsible for inputs and outputs. This could lead to unforeseen consequences if users don't fully understand AI-generated content.
* **Sublicensable license:** TikTok may sublicense the user's content for training its AI/ML systems, which could lead to their content being used in ways they didn't intend or agree to.
source_tos:
SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — TIKTOK TERMS OF SERVICE (US) (Effective 2026; replaces the 2023 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with TikTok and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2026 version differs from the 2023 version in the following ways: Effective January 22, 2026: contracting party changed to TikTok USDS following the US joint venture; added explicit generative-AI rules (output 'as is', user responsibility for inputs/outputs, prohibition on stripping watermarks or claiming AI output is human-made); reaffirmed sublicensable license to use content for training ML models.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by TikTok to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://www.tiktok.com/legal/page/us/terms-of-service/en . The previous version is available at https://web.archive.org/web/20231101000000*/https://www.tiktok.com/legal/page/us/terms-of-service/en .

Here's a plain-language summary:

**Service Name**: Adobe General Terms of Use
**Effective Date**: 2024 (replaces 2023 version)

**Key Provisions:**

* **Scope**: These terms govern your relationship with Adobe and apply to their products and services listed on their official terms page.
* **Content and License**: Adobe uses user-submitted content to operate, improve, and train their AI/ML systems, subject to your settings and applicable laws.
* **Privacy**: The terms refer to Adobe's published Privacy Policy, which outlines the types of personal data collected and how it's processed.
* **Dispute Resolution**: The terms require binding arbitration, which means private dispute resolution instead of going to court. Class-action lawsuits are also waived. You have a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts.
* **Termination**: Either party can terminate the agreement under specific conditions.
* **Contact**: For questions about these terms, contact Adobe through their published legal contact information.

**Harmful Clauses to Consider:**

* **Access to user content**: Adobe can access your content through automated and manual methods to improve services and software. This could be a concern for users who don't want their data used in specific ways.
* **Generative AI models**: While Adobe states they don't train generative-AI models on customer cloud content, this might not be a complete reassurance for users who are concerned about AI data usage.
* **Binding arbitration**: This means you won't be able to bring a class-action lawsuit against Adobe. However, you can opt-out of arbitration within 30 days of creating a new account.
* **Opt-out window**: If you create a new account, you must opt-out of binding arbitration within 30 days to keep your right to litigate in a court of law.

Please review the terms carefully and consider how they might affect your specific situation. If you have questions or concerns, contact Adobe through their published contact information.
source_tos:
SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — ADOBE GENERAL TERMS OF USE (Effective 2024; replaces the 2023 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with Adobe and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2024 version differs from the 2023 version in the following ways: February 2024 update added language allowing Adobe to access user content via 'automated and manual methods' to improve services and software. After backlash in June 2024, Adobe rewrote sections in clearer language, explicitly stating it does not train generative-AI models on customer cloud content and added a plain-English summary of changes.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by Adobe to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://www.adobe.com/legal/terms.html . The previous version is available at https://web.archive.org/web/20231101000000*/https://www.adobe.com/legal/terms.html .

**Service Name:** LinkedIn User Agreement

**Summary:** These Terms of Service (TOS) outline the rules and guidelines for users of LinkedIn's products and services. The agreement is between you, the user, and LinkedIn. It explains how you can use LinkedIn's services, how LinkedIn uses your data, and how you can resolve disputes.

**Key Provisions:**

* **What you can do on LinkedIn:** The TOS governs your relationship with LinkedIn and apply to the products and services they offer.
* **Use of your data:** Your user-submitted content can be used by LinkedIn to operate, improve, and train their AI/ML systems.
* **Data protection:** The TOS cross-references LinkedIn's Privacy Policy, which outlines the types of personal data collected and how it's processed.
* **Dispute resolution:** You're required to participate in binding arbitration (a private dispute process instead of court) with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts.
* **Termination:** Either party can terminate the agreement under certain conditions.

**Potential Red Flags:**

* **Use of member data for AI training:** While LinkedIn provides an opt-out toggle in Settings for this practice, some users may find it concerning that their data is being used to train AI models. **(Please note: this is a summary; it's essential to review the actual TOS for specific details.)**
* **Binding arbitration requirements:** The agreement requires users to participate in arbitration over disputes, which may limit your ability to pursue court action. **(Note: the arbitration provision also includes a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts.)**
source_tos:
SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — LINKEDIN USER AGREEMENT (Effective 2024; replaces the 2023 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with LinkedIn and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2024 version differs from the 2023 version in the following ways: November 20, 2024 update added explicit references to use of member data and content to train generative AI models for LinkedIn features (with an opt-out toggle in Settings). Also updated dispute-resolution and class-action waiver provisions.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by LinkedIn to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://www.linkedin.com/legal/user-agreement . The previous version is available at https://www.linkedin.com/legal/previous-user-agreement .

**Service Name:** The updated Terms of Service (TOS) govern the relationship between you and Discord, a company providing products and services on its official terms page.

**Key Provisions:**

1. **Scope:** These terms apply to the products and services mentioned on Discord's official terms page.
2. **Content and License:** Discord uses your submitted content to operate, improve, and train its AI/ML systems, in accordance with your settings and applicable law.
3. **Privacy:** The company's published Privacy Policy explains how personal data is collected and processed. You can find this information separately.
4. **Dispute Resolution:** You agree to binding arbitration (a private dispute process instead of court) with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts. Some users may be exempt (e.g., those using Steam, which has removed mandatory arbitration).
5. **Termination:** Either party can terminate the agreement under specific conditions described in the live document.
6. **Contact:** For questions about these terms, visit Discord's published legal contact information.

**Harmful Clauses:**

* **Binding arbitration (Dispute Resolution):** While providing a convenient dispute resolution process, this clause forces users into private arbitration instead of taking their grievances to court. This can limit your ability to pursue class-action lawsuits or seek judicial review.

Note that by using the service, you acknowledge having read and agreed to these terms. Remember to review Discord's Privacy Policy for more detailed information on personal data collection and processing.
source_tos:
SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — DISCORD TERMS OF SERVICE (Effective 2025; replaces the 2024 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with Discord and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2025 version differs from the 2024 version in the following ways: August 2025 update modernized arbitration language, added new sections on AI-generated content and Discord's use of metadata to train safety systems, expanded the Paid Service Terms, and refreshed Community Guidelines references. Summary: discord.com/safety/important-policy-updates.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by Discord to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://discord.com/terms . The previous version is available at https://web.archive.org/web/20240601000000*/https://discord.com/terms .

**Summary of GitHub Terms of Service**

The official name of this agreement is the GitHub Terms of Service.

Let's break down the key provisions:

* **Scope**: These terms apply to your relationship with GitHub and affect how you use the company's products and services.
* **Content and License**: You grant GitHub permission to use your submission, subject to your settings and applicable law. You need to understand how your content is used to improve their operations and AI/ML systems.
* **Privacy**: Your personal data is handled according to GitHub's published **Privacy Policy**. It's essential to review this policy to understand how your data is collected and processed.
* **Dispute Resolution**: In case of disputes, you and GitHub agree to use **binding arbitration** (a private dispute process instead of going to court) with **class-action waivers**. This means you'll give up the right to join a group lawsuit. However, you have a 30-day **opt-out window** for new accounts if you don't agree.

Harmful clause: `Dispute Resolution` and `Binding Arbitration`
The fact that binding arbitration with class-action waivers is mandatory may harm users who cannot afford private arbitration costs or want to join class-action lawsuits. 

* **Termination**: Either you or GitHub can end the agreement. Review the document to see the conditions.
* **Contact**: For questions regarding these terms, please visit the company's published contact information.

Please note that this is a summary of the Terms of Service, and it's your responsibility to review the document carefully before agreeing.

SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — GITHUB TERMS OF SERVICE (Effective 2026; replaces the 2024 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with GitHub and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2026 version differs from the 2024 version in the following ways: March 2026 update expanded the Affiliates section so personal data may be shared with Microsoft and other GitHub affiliates for AI/ML model development, added a new product-development purpose for using personal data to train AI features, and clarified that user opt-out preferences propagate to affiliates.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by GitHub to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://docs.github.com/en/site-policy/github-terms/github-terms-of-service . The previous version is available at https://web.archive.org/web/20240101000000*/https://docs.github.com/en/site-policy/github-terms/github-terms-of-service .

**Service Name:** Disney+ Subscriber Agreement

**Key Provisions:**

* **Scope:** These terms and conditions govern your relationship with Disney+, covering the services and products described on Disney+'s official terms page.
* **Content and License:** Disney+ may use your submitted content to improve its AI/ML systems, subject to your settings and applicable law.
* **Privacy:** Disney+ cross-references its published Privacy Policy, which details the types of personal data collected and how it's processed.
* **Dispute Resolution:** Any disputes will be resolved through binding arbitration, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts. This means you'll give up your right to a trial by court and may be required to settle disputes privately.
* **Termination:** Either party can terminate the agreement under certain conditions.

**Harmful Clauses:**

* **Forced arbitration**: The dispute resolution process may be harmful if you feel you've been wronged by Disney+. Arbitration can be biased and may not provide the same protections as a court trial.
* **Class-action waiver**: You may give up your right to participate in class-action lawsuits, which can be more effective in bringing attention to widespread issues.
* **Advertising on ad-free plans**: As of January 27, 2025, Disney+ may begin showing ads on its "no ads" or "ad-free" tiers, which could affect the value of these plans.

**Note:** The Terms of Service do not explicitly address topics such as:

* The potential use of AI-generated content
* Data security in case of a breach
* The specific types of data collected and stored by Disney+

If you're concerned about these or other aspects, it's recommended to review Disney+'s Privacy Policy and contact their legal team for clarification.
source_tos:
SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — DISNEY+ SUBSCRIBER AGREEMENT (Effective 2025; replaces the 2024 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with Disney+ and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2025 version differs from the 2024 version in the following ways: Effective January 27, 2025 for new subscribers and March 24, 2025 for existing ones: streaming titles may now show ads even on 'no ads'/'ad free' tiers, expanded arbitration with mass-arbitration procedures following Disney's earlier 2024 Wrongful-Death-case controversy, and updated content-availability language.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by Disney+ to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://www.disneyplus.com/legal/subscriber-agreement . The previous version is available at https://web.archive.org/web/20240101000000*/https://www.disneyplus.com/legal/subscriber-agreement .

**Service Name:** PayPal User Agreement

**Summary:**

These Terms of Service outline the relationship between you and PayPal, the provider of online payment services. The main points of the agreement are:

* **Scope:** These terms apply to PayPal services and products described on their official terms page.
* **Content and License:** PayPal uses user-submitted content, if necessary, to function and improve their services. This content can be used in AI/ML systems.
* **Privacy:** The Privacy Policy, linked within these terms, explains what personal data PayPal collects and how it's processed.
* **Dispute Resolution:** In case of disputes, they primarily require binding arbitration (a private dispute process instead of court), with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts.
* **Termination:** Either party can end the agreement under specific conditions.
* **Contact:** For questions, see PayPal's published legal contact information.

Some key provisions to consider:
- **Arbitration**: While optional, binding arbitration (a private dispute process) with class-action waivers may limit your ability to join a class-action lawsuit. A 30-day opt-out window for new accounts allows you to opt out of this condition.
- **Data usage**: PayPal may use submitted content to improve their services and AI/ML systems. This data might include personal or financial information.
- **Termination**: Termination can occur if either party breaches conditions or due to unforeseen events, such as regulatory changes.

Keep in mind that binding arbitration can limit your ability to seek redress through the courts and that data usage can raise concerns about data protection. However, these points are standard in many online services agreements. If you have explicit concerns or need further information about these points, consider reviewing PayPal's Privacy Policy and their user agreement closely.
source_tos:
SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — PAYPAL USER AGREEMENT (Effective 2024; replaces the 2023 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with PayPal and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2024 version differs from the 2023 version in the following ways: Multiple 2024 updates: revised seller-protection criteria, added new fee schedules for cross-border transactions, expanded the dispute resolution / chargeback flow, and clarified handling of cryptocurrency holdings. PayPal publishes upcoming and historical policy diffs at paypal.com/us/legalhub/policy-updates.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by PayPal to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).

response:
**Service Name: Apple Media Services Terms and Conditions**

These Terms of Service govern your relationship with Apple when using their media services, such as iCloud, Apple Music, and the App Store.

**Key Provisions:**

* **Scope:** These terms apply to all Apple media services you use.
* **Content and License:** Apple can use your submitted content to improve and train their AI systems, but only with your settings and applicable law in mind.
* **Privacy:** Apple's Privacy Policy sets out how they collect and process your personal data.
* **Dispute Resolution:** In case of a dispute, you'll need to go through binding arbitration (a private dispute process instead of court), with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts.
* **Termination:** Apple or you can terminate the agreement, subject to the conditions described in the document.

**Noteworthy Clauses:**

* **Binding Arbitration:** Requiring arbitration means you might waive your right to sue Apple in court. While this can be a faster and cheaper process, it might limit your options if you feel Apple has wronged you. 
* **Class-Action Waivers:** You might also be waiving your right to join a class-action lawsuit with others who have similar claims against Apple.
* **Termination:** Apple can terminate the agreement at any time, which might leave you without access to their services.

Overall, these Terms of Service outline how Apple uses your content and personal data, and how they resolve disputes. While they don't explicitly state any clauses that are harmful to users, the arbitration and class-action waiver requirements are worth considering carefully.
source_tos:
SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — APPLE MEDIA SERVICES TERMS AND CONDITIONS (Effective 2024; replaces the 2023 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with Apple and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2024 version differs from the 2023 version in the following ways: 2024 update added explicit references to Apple Intelligence and on-device generative-AI features, clarified content-license scope across services (iCloud, Apple Music, App Store), and revised Family Sharing and Subscriptions sections.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by Apple to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://www.apple.com/legal/internet-services/itunes/us/terms.html . The previous version is available at https://web.archive.org/web/20230101000000*/https://www.apple.com/legal/internet-services/itunes/us/terms.html .

The service name is iCloud Terms and Conditions. Here's a plain-language summary:

**Service Overview**
iCloud is a cloud storage service provided by Apple. These Terms of Service (TOS) explain how Apple will use your data, what you're allowed to do with the service, and under what circumstances the service can be terminated.

**Key Provisions**

* **Content Submission**: When you use iCloud, Apple may collect content you submit (e.g., photos, emails, documents). Apple can use this content to improve its services, operate its business, or train its AI/ML systems. This is subject to your settings and applicable law.
* **Data Protection**: The Privacy Policy governs Apple's collection and processing of personal data. You can find the Privacy Policy document separately.
* **Terms and Dispute Resolution**: Apple may terminate your account at any time, and you can also terminate the agreement with 30 days' notice (subject to certain conditions). To resolve disputes, you're required to participate in binding arbitration, which is a private dispute process instead of going to court. However, if you create a new account, you have a 30-day opt-out window. (This might be considered a bit restrictive, potentially limiting users' options to resolve disputes.)
* **Legal and Safety Exceptions**: Apple may access your stored content under certain circumstances, such as when necessary for safety or legal reasons.
* **Termination**: Either you or Apple can end the agreement by giving notice.

**Harmful Clauses**

* **Binding Arbitration**: This might limit your options to resolve disputes, as it requires you to participate in a private process instead of going to court. However, new account holders have a 30-day opt-out window.
* **Class-Action Waiver**: Apple does not permit you to join a group action lawsuit against the company, which might limit your options to recover damages.
* **Retention of Rights**: Apple can access your content in specific circumstances and retains rights to use such content without asking for your permission.

**Notable Notes**

* The document was last updated in 2024.
* These terms are subject to change (as seen in the Summary of Updated Terms of Service).
* Apple provides contact information at the bottom of the document for questions and concerns about these terms.
source_tos:
SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — ICLOUD TERMS AND CONDITIONS (Effective 2024; replaces the 2022 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with Apple and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2024 version differs from the 2022 version in the following ways: 2024 update added Advanced Data Protection (end-to-end encryption) language, references to Apple Intelligence Private Cloud Compute, and revised provisions about how stored content may be accessed by Apple for legal/safety reasons.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by Apple to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://www.apple.com/legal/internet-services/icloud/en/terms.html . The previous version is available at https://web.archive.org/web/20220101000000*/https://www.apple.com/legal/internet-services/icloud/en/terms.html .

**Summary of Canva Terms of Use:**

The Canva Terms of Use govern your relationship with Canva and apply to the products and services offered on the Canva website. The updated terms, effective 2024, outline agreements between Canva and its users.

**Key Provisions:**

* **Scope:** These terms apply to all Canva products and services listed on the company's official terms page.
* **Content and License:** When you submit content to Canva, you agree to how it's used by the company to operate and improve its services.
* **Ownership:** If you use Canva's generative AI tools (such as Magic Studio), you own any output you create, but Canva may still hold some rights to it.
* **Privacy:** Canva's published Privacy Policy explains how your personal data is collected and processed.
* **Termination:** Either party can cancel the agreement under specified conditions.

Potential Concerns:

* **Content Moderation:** As part of using Canva's AI tools, there are new requirements for content-moderation and labeling.
* **Arbitration:** The terms require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, although there's a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts. Arbitration means using a private dispute resolution process instead of going to court.
* **Restrictions on AI Use:** You are not allowed to use Canva-generated content to train other AI models.

Note: These potential concerns may seem complex, but we can discuss them further if you have any questions.
source_tos:
SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — CANVA TERMS OF USE (Effective 2024; replaces the 2023 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with Canva and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2024 version differs from the 2023 version in the following ways: 2024 update added rules for Canva's generative AI tools (Magic Studio): users own outputs subject to platform rights, restrictions on using Canva-generated content to train other AI models, and new content-moderation/labeling requirements.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by Canva to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://www.canva.com/policies/terms-of-use/ . The previous version is available at https://web.archive.org/web/20230101000000*/https://www.canva.com/policies/terms-of-use/ .

These are the Terms of Service for Notion, a productivity and note-taking service. 

**Key Provisions:**

* The Terms of Service describe the rules and guidelines for using Notion services, which includes using Notion's products and services.
* When using Notion, you grant them the right to use your submitted content to operate, improve, and train their AI/ML systems, subject to your settings and applicable laws.
* The service emphasizes that they collect personal data from their users, which is governed by Notion's Privacy Policy. 
* Any disputes will be resolved through binding arbitration (a private dispute process instead of court), and users may opt-out within 30 days for new accounts (exceptions apply).
* Either party can terminate the agreement according to conditions stated in the document.

**Harmful Clauses:**

* **Binding Arbitration**: This means that in the event of a dispute, you'll have to resolve it privately through arbitration, rather than going to court. Some users may consider this restrictive or potentially unfair to their interests.
* **Class-Action Waivers**: This clause means that if there's a dispute, you won't be able to join a group of people with similar complaints against Notion. This can limit your options for seeking justice.
* **Termination**: Notion can terminate your account subject to conditions described in the document. This means that Notion can remove your content, and you may lose access to any data you've stored on their platform.
source_tos:
SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — NOTION TERMS OF SERVICE (Effective 2024; replaces the 2023 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with Notion and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2024 version differs from the 2023 version in the following ways: 2024 update added Notion AI provisions (input/output ownership, no training of foundational models on customer data by default), updated subprocessor list, and clarified data-residency options for enterprise plans.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by Notion to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://www.notion.com/terms . The previous version is available at https://web.archive.org/web/20230101000000*/https://www.notion.so/terms .

**Service Name:** Figma

**Key Provisions:**

These Terms of Service outline the relationship between Figma and users. Here are the key points:

* **Scope**: These terms govern how Figma uses its products and services.
* **Content and License**: Figma uses user-submitted content to improve and train its AI and machine learning (ML) systems, but only with your settings and applicable law.
* **Content is used to train AI/ML systems**: User content may be used to train AI and ML systems, including third-party models. However, Figma states that they will only do so with opt-in.
* **Privacy**: The company refers to its published Privacy Policy to explain how personal data is collected and processed.
* **Dispute Resolution**: Most terms require binding arbitration with class-action waivers. This means that any disputes would go to a private process instead of court (see [binding arbitration](#)).
* **Termination**: Either Figma or the user can terminate the agreement if the live document's conditions are met.

**Clauses to be aware of:**

*  **Figma may use third-party AI models**: Figma states that they will only use third-party generative models with opt-in. However, users should be aware that this may change in the future.
* **No guarantees about AI/ML training**: Although Figma says they'll use opt-in for third-party models, they don't explicitly state what happens to content beyond their own systems.
* **No court representation**: Binding arbitration (a private dispute process)(#) can be detrimental to users, especially if they have limited financial resources or power against large corporations.

**Notes:**
If you have any concerns about your rights or the potential impact of these Terms of Service, it might be best to consult a legal professional. These notes are based on the provided version of the terms.
source_tos:
SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — FIGMA TERMS OF SERVICE (Effective 2024; replaces the 2023 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with Figma and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2024 version differs from the 2023 version in the following ways: 2024 update added Figma AI features (Make Designs, Visual Search) provisions, clarified that customer file content is not used to train third-party generative models without opt-in, and updated security and incident-notification language.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by Figma to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://www.figma.com/legal/tos/ . The previous version is available at https://web.archive.org/web/20230101000000*/https://www.figma.com/tos/ .

response:
The service is called the Stack Overflow Public Network Terms of Service, and these terms outline the agreement between you and Stack Overflow when using their products and services.

**Key Provisions:**

* These terms apply to the products and services described on Stack Overflow's official terms page.
* When you post content, like questions and answers, on Stack Overflow, it can be used by the company to operate, improve, and train their AI/ML systems, depending on your settings and applicable law.
* Your personal data is collected and processed as described in Stack Overflow's published Privacy Policy.

**Important Clauses:**

* You grant Stack Overflow a license to use your posted content, specifically under the Creative Commons Attribution-ShareAlike (CC BY-SA) license.
* However, there are restrictions on using or extracting the content for training generative AI or LLMs without a commercial agreement with the company. This means you might not be allowed to use Stack Overflow content for certain AI training purposes unless you have a specific agreement with them.
* If you have a dispute with Stack Overflow, you and the company agree to binding arbitration (a private dispute process instead of going to court) with class-action waivers, unless you opt out within 30 days of creating your account.
* Either Stack Overflow or you can terminate the agreement, subject to the conditions described in the live document.

**Potential Harm:**

* The restriction on using Stack Overflow content for AI training without a commercial agreement might limit your ability to use their content for certain AI applications.
* The binding arbitration clause with class-action waivers may not allow you to join a class-action lawsuit against Stack Overflow, potentially limiting your ability to seek redress for certain grievances.
source_tos:
SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — STACK OVERFLOW PUBLIC NETWORK TERMS OF SERVICE (Effective 2024; replaces the 2023 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with Stack Overflow and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2024 version differs from the 2023 version in the following ways: May 2024 update added a 'Generative AI / LLM' restriction explicitly licensing posted Q&A under CC BY-SA but limiting bulk extraction for AI training without a commercial agreement, after the company's content-licensing deals with OpenAI and Google.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by Stack Overflow to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://stackoverflow.com/legal/terms-of-service/public . The previous version is available at https://web.archive.org/web/20230101000000*/https://stackoverflow.com/legal/terms-of-service/public .

**Service Name:** 23andMe Terms of Service

**Key Provisions:**

The 23andMe Terms of Service govern the relationship between 23andMe and its users. Here's a breakdown of key points:

* **Scope:** These terms apply to the products and services described on 23andMe's official terms page.
* **Content and License:** 23andMe uses user-submitted content to operate, improve, and train its AI and ML systems, in accordance with user settings and applicable law.
* **Privacy:** The terms reference 23andMe's published **Privacy Policy**, which outlines the types of personal data collected and how it is processed.
* **Dispute Resolution:** Most disputes need to go through **binding arbitration**, where users waive the right to class-action lawsuits and have a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts. 
* **Termination:** Either party can terminate the agreement based on conditions outlined in the live document.

**Clauses That May Be Harmful to Users:**

* **Mandatory Arbitration Clause:** If you don't opt out, you'll have to go through binding arbitration for certain disputes, which may limit your rights to sue for breach-related claims. This includes a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts.
* **Class Action Waivers:** By agreeing to these terms, you give up your right to join or participate in class-action lawsuits against 23andMe.

These changes may affect users who don't write to opt out or take action within the stated timeframe.
source_tos:
SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — 23ANDME TERMS OF SERVICE (Effective 2023; replaces the 2022 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with 23andMe and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2023 version differs from the 2022 version in the following ways: After the October 2023 data breach, 23andMe updated its TOS to add a mandatory-arbitration clause and 30-day opt-out window, requiring users who didn't write to opt out to arbitrate any breach-related claims; also limited class-action rights and shortened the dispute-notice window.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by 23andMe to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://www.23andme.com/legal/terms-of-service/ . The previous version is available at https://www.23andme.com/legal/terms-of-service/full-version/2.0/ .

It's essential to note that these Terms of Service may change, and users should review them regularly to stay informed about any updates or changes.

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with Twitch and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2024 version differs from the 2023 version in the following ways: 2024 update added new Branded Content disclosure rules, expanded the User Content license to support clips, replays and AI-generated highlights, and updated the dispute-resolution mass-arbitration procedure.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by Twitch to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://www.twitch.tv/p/legal/terms-of-service/ . The previous version is available at https://web.archive.org/web/20230101000000*/https://www.twitch.tv/p/legal/terms-of-service/ .
